title: explainer-signature/v3
description: nodes/<id>/explainer/signed/<hash>-<n>.yaml (F15-R8; D-3 v3.17): a real-identity contributor's signature on one explainer, affirming one sentence — I can explain this proof without the tool that produced it. It claims nothing about the mathematics, changes no verdict and earns nothing at merge; only signed explainers count toward a resolved target's digestion state (D-33 v3.17). Signed with the signer's own SSH key (SSHSIG, opn_gate.signed) over the canonical body, the document without `signature`. v2 adds sections: a signature approves the sections it names (F21-R13, D-3 v3.31).  v3 adds `via` (F23-R10, R11; D-3 v3.33): the signature may be made through the service with the network's approval key for a signed-in steward or curator, and means what an SSH signature means. Versioned, never edited (D-34).

explainer.description: The SHA-256 of the explainer file the signature is on — its name under explainer/ (D-3: content-hashed). A signature whose explainer is absent is refused by name.

affirmation.description: The fixed sentence, verbatim (opn_gate.explainers.AFFIRMATION). Any other text is refused.

signer.description: The signer's GitHub login. At Stage 0 a real-identity contributor is an active steward of the target or a listed curator (F15-Q4).

via.description: How the signature was made (D-3, D-32 v3.33): `ssh`, by the signer's own SSH key; `approval-key`, by the network's approval key through the service, for a login signed in with GitHub on the site, in which case `key` must equal the graph's keys/approval.pub in the merge's parent tree.

sections.description: The sections this signature approves and verifies (F21-R13; D-3 v3.31), by key; absent approves every section of the version.

items.description: A section's key (F21-R11): overview for an explainer's unanchored first section, whole for a gloss, else steps: and the section's step ids, sorted, comma-separated.
